summary: Long-lived client connections causing API gateway accept-queue starvation and upstream runtime crashloop with elevated 5xx
description:
Issue summary:
Customer QueryWell reported a rapid increase in 5xx responses starting 2026-03-12 10:20 UTC for production traffic routed to their dedicated pool. Symptoms include API gateway 502/503 spikes coincident with long-lived streaming connections from a handful of client IPs. Upstream runtimes entered crashloop/eviction cycles and GPU memory fragmentation grew steadily during the window.

Impact:
- QueryWell observed ~18% of requests returning 5xx over a 40-minute period, primarily streaming endpoints.
- Latency increased for non-streaming requests by ~30%.
- Incident impacted a single dedicated pool (customer-dedicated) — no cross-customer outage reported.

Environment:
- prod/us-east (customer dedicated capacity)
- Affected runtimes: r10-r16 in dedicated pool qwe-us-east-02
- Models in use: redwood-alpha-13b-q4 (inference with KV cache and streaming enabled)

Steps to reproduce (as observed):
1) Customer opens many long-lived streaming sessions (keepalive) from ~8 client hosts.
2) Several sessions are not cleanly closed (client-side abrupt disconnects), leaving half-open streams.
3) API gateway accept queue depth climbs; accept-queue backlog growth is visible on edge metrics.
4) Serving runtime experiences elevated socket backlog and increases memory fragmentation; GPU allocator hits fragmentation threshold causing occasional out-of-memory reclamation and process restart.
5) Upstream restarts cause immediate 502/503 responses until new workers spin up and prefetch completes.

Observed logs / metrics snippets: 
- apigw.accept_queue_depth spike to 962 at 2026-03-12T10:26Z
- edge.stream_sessions.active (customer-dedicated) increased from 120 -> 840 in 12 minutes
- runtime.gpu.fragmentation_pct rising from 12% -> 68% before evictions
- runtime.process.exit_reason: OOM_RECLAIM at 2026-03-12T10:33Z
- apigw.5xx_rate customer-dedicated: baseline 0.2% -> 18%

Attachments: collected tcpdump (partial), apigw and runtime graphs, sample logs from runtime r13, client connection list exported by edge service.
investigation_notes: 10:28 UTC - Support acknowledged customer signal and opened incident; triage to SRE and Runtime oncall.
10:35 UTC - Observed tight correlation between long-lived streams and accept-queue growth; single customer IP range responsible for ~65% of long-lived sessions.
10:45 UTC - Runtime oncall identified repeated gpu allocator OOM_RECLAIM cycles; worker restarts coincident with apigw 502 spikes.

11:00 UTC - Hypothesis: incomplete client shutdowns + aggressive keepalive behavior caused accept-queue starvation which increased per-worker socket state and prevented normal KV cache warmup, gradually fragmenting GPU memory and triggering OOM reclamation.
11:12 UTC - Validated via heapmaps and nvml counters: fragmentation increased in affected runtimes, unaffected runtimes in same zone stayed stable.

11:25 UTC - Applied temporary ingress mitigation: limited concurrent streaming sessions per-customer-IP and increased apigw accept queue threshold; observed immediate reduction in new half-open streams.
12:00 UTC - After mitigation, runtime restarts frequency dropped and 5xx rate declined to ~1.8% within 35 minutes.
Next steps: implement longer-term circuit (backpressure + client throttling), add detection alert for per-customer long-lived stream explosion, and coordinate with QueryWell to patch client behavior.
comments: Ava Chen (Support) 2026-03-12 10:30 UTC: Initial customer report attached tcpdump and said errors started after a traffic ramp of streaming sessions.
Samir Rao (SRE) 2026-03-12 10:38 UTC: Looking at apigw metrics now; accept_queue_depth is spiking. Routing to runtime oncall @Raj.

Raj Patel (Runtime oncall) 2026-03-12 10:46 UTC: Found repeated OOM_RECLAIM in r13 and r14; collecting nvml and allocator traces. Suspect fragmentation from many small persistent tensors in streaming session lifecycle.
Customer (QueryWell) 2026-03-12 11:05 UTC: Their SDK opened persistent streams to support interactive dashboarding; confirmed a recent client-side SDK update that changed reconnect semantics.
Raj Patel 2026-03-12 11:28 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied (ingress concurrent-stream cap and accept-queue tuning). Seeing 5xx rate trending down.
Ava Chen 2026-03-12 12:05 UTC: Shared mitigation steps and timeline with customer; they will revert the SDK change and re-test. Will monitor for 24 hours.
Support note 2026-03-13 09:00 UTC: Follow-up requested to implement alerting for long-lived stream spikes and a runtime patch to compact small allocator fragments more aggressively on restart.
resolution:
Workaround applied: per-IP concurrent streaming cap and accept-queue threshold increase reduced the new half-open streams; customer rolled back the SDK change that left sessions half-open. Runtime restarts declined and 5xx rate dropped to near-baseline in ~35 minutes.

Planned permanent fix: (1) introduce an automated per-tenant streaming explosion detection and ingress backpressure rule; (2) runtime change to defragment allocator proactively during low-traffic windows and add a safety eviction path before OOM_RECLAIM; (3) update runbook with client SDK guidance.

Follow-ups assigned: Raj to author runtime PR for allocator defrag (ETA 2 weeks), SRE to add alert and playbook (ETA 3 days), Support to coordinate with QueryWell on client SDK best-practices (ETA 1 day).
